samples.summary: Gate 1b's `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` is far narrower than the CI-defining surface it claims to cover — a branch can gut CI via `package.json` / `scripts/verify-*.mjs` / `harness.config.json` and still auto-promote, while the new hand-off comment tells the human reviewer the run executed main's CI definition.
samples.evidence: Gate 1b refuses promotion only when a changed path starts with `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` (mark-ready.mjs:175, 189). But `ci.yml` contains almost no test logic: `verify-self` runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:308) and `verify-integration` runs `pnpm verify:integration` (ci.yml:752), both resolved from the MERGE REF's `package.json` ("verify:self": "node ./scripts/verify-self.mjs", package.json:25) and executed from the branch's `scripts/verify-self.mjs`. The `changes` job likewise runs the branch's `node ./scripts/changed-areas.mjs` (ci.yml:149) and its `heavy` output gates every step of `verify-browser` / `verify-integration` / coverage (ci.yml:317-321, 484-487, 593-596). ATTACK: under gate 1b's own stated threat model ("an `agent:managed` human PR is on this promote path and is not restricted", mark-ready.mjs:28), the author pushes a commit that changes only `scripts/verify-self.mjs` (or the `verify:self` script in `package.json`, or `harness.config.json` so `heavy=false`) so the lanes no-op. `.github/workflows/**` is untouched, so `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes, gate 1 sees a genuinely green run of the genuine `ci.yml`, and the PR is auto-promoted. The repo already knows the real surface: `harness.config.json`'s `ciConfig` list (harness.config.json:52-62) names `harness.config.json`, `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, `scripts/verify-*.mjs`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `knip.json` alongside `.github/workflows/**` — gate 1b uses none of them, and `ciConfig` only forces a full run rather than refusing promotion. The harm is amplified rather than mitigated by this delta: the hand-off comment now asserts "the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on `main` rather than one the branch supplied" (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) and the design doc's honest "WHAT THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE" paragraph was replaced with "Gate 1b closes that" (mark-ready.mjs:19) — a gate that reads as covered to the human who is the last real merge gate.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's evidence (`pulls/{n}/files`) is diffed against the PR's BASE ref, which the PR author can change at will and which is not pinned to the SHA gate 1 read — retargeting the base after CI starts empties the file list and lets a workflow-editing branch through.
samples.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` asks `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files` (mark-ready.mjs:183), which returns the base..head diff for the PR's CURRENT base branch — a mutable, author-controlled field — whereas gate 1's evidence is a CI run pinned to `pr.headRefOid` (mark-ready.mjs:158, 166). ATTACK (same threat model as the gate: a collaborator opening an `agent:managed` PR): (1) push branch `x` containing a gutted `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; (2) open the PR from that head against `main`, so CI's `pull_request: branches: ["main"]` trigger (ci.yml:9-10) fires and runs the branch's gutted `ci.yml` on the merge ref, concluding green; the panel starts on `workflow_run: requested` and `promote` waits for the conclusion (agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1462); (3) before the promote job runs `mark-ready`, retarget the PR's base to another branch in the same repo that already carries the same gutted `ci.yml`. Retargeting neither cancels the already-created CI run nor changes `headRefOid`, so gate 1 still reads `success` — but `pulls/{n}/files` now diffs against the new base and reports no `.github/workflows/**` entry, so gate 1b passes and the PR is promoted with the hand-off comment claiming main's CI definition ran. A slower variant needs no race: retarget after the refusal, then `@claude rerun`, whose `workflow_run: completed` with `run_attempt > 1` is explicitly admitted by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169). I could not execute this to confirm GitHub does not cancel the in-flight run on retarget, hence medium confidence. A base-independent check (e.g. comparing the head tree's `.github/workflows/**` against the default branch, or reading the run's own `head_sha` tree) would not have this property.

samples.summary: The staged `trigger-shape` canary echoes attacker-influenced `workflow_run.name` / `path` straight into `::error::` workflow commands, which is a (low-impact) workflow-command injection sink the maintainer is being asked to apply verbatim.
samples.evidence: The patch's step passes `WF_NAME: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.name }}` and `WF_PATH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.path }}` via `env:` (correct — no expression interpolation into the shell) but then writes them into `echo "::error::A run named '$WF_NAME' came from '$WF_PATH' ..."`. Both values come from a workflow file's `name:` key / filename, i.e. from whoever added the second same-repo workflow the canary exists to report — precisely the adversary in its own threat model. A value containing a newline plus `::` lets that actor emit arbitrary GitHub workflow commands (`::add-mask::`, `::notice::`, `::stop-commands::`) into the job log. Impact is small because the job inherits the file's top-level `permissions: {}` and has no outputs or downstream consumers, so this is hardening only: prefer `printf '%s\n'` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`/stderr, or strip `::`/newlines, rather than `echo "::error::..."` with untrusted content.
searchedFor: read the full patch hunk under review

verdict.reason: Code is exactly as described. `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` (mark-ready.mjs:175) covers only `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`, and line 189 is the sole path test in `branchEditsCiDefinition`. But CI's substance comes from the merge ref's own scripts: ci.yml:289 checks out the merge ref with a plain checkout, ci.yml:308 runs `pnpm verify:self` -> `node ./scripts/verify-self.mjs` (package.json:25), ci.yml:149 runs the branch's `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, and its `heavy` output gates the heavy/coverage steps (ci.yml:317-321). A branch editing only `scripts/verify-self.mjs`, the `verify:self` script in `package.json`, or `harness.config.json` therefore produces a genuinely green run of the genuine `ci.yml` with nothing verified, while gate 1b returns false-for-edits and lets auto-promotion proceed (agent-review-panel.yml:1462-1508 invokes `--promote` on gate pass). The repo's own `ciConfig` list (harness.config.json:52-62) enumerates exactly these paths but, per ciConfigReason (line 51), only forces a full run — it never refuses promotion, so it is not a guard here. The hand-off comment (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) then asserts to the human reviewer that the run executed main's CI definition, so the gate reads as covered when it is not. In-lane (weakened/bypassable gate on the enforced promotion path) and blocking as a major security weakness; I could not find any guard or caller that makes it unreachable.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present exactly as described. mark-ready.mjs:183 sources gate 1b's evidence from `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files`, which is a base..head diff against the PR's CURRENT base ref — an author-mutable field — while gate 1 (mark-ready.mjs:156-166) pins its evidence to `pr.headRefOid` via `actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=`. The two gates are therefore anchored to independently mutable things, and retargeting the base after the CI run exists shrinks or empties the file list without invalidating the pinned run. No guard closes this: `pr view --json` at mark-ready.mjs:127 never even fetches the base ref, and a tree-wide grep for baseRefName/baseRefOid/base_ref finds consumers only in scripts/agent/eval/extract-corpus.mjs and scripts/changed-areas.mjs, nothing on the promote path. The promote job (agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1508) gates only on ci conclusion and panel outputs, then invokes mark-ready directly with no base validation. The re-entry vector is real too: agent-review-panel.yml:164-169 explicitly admits `run_attempt > 1` completed events, so the slow `@claude rerun` variant needs no race. The threat model is the script's own stated one (header lines 16-29: an `agent:managed` human PR is on this promote path unrestricted, and a pull_request run executes the merge ref's copy of ci.yml). None of the three refutation grounds apply — the code is present, unguarded, and this is an authorization/gate-integrity defect squarely in the security lane. Impact is bounded to false promotion plus a hand-off comment (lines 313-329) falsely asserting main's CI definition ran, not a merge, so major is the right severity; that does not make it non-blocking under the added-but-bypassable-gate rubric.

finding.summary: Gate 1 verifies WHICH workflow file ran but not WHAT was in it — an `agent:managed` PR branch can supply its own gutted `ci.yml` and get a genuinely green run at the genuine path
finding.evidence: `ciPassed()` (mark-ready.mjs:140-160) asks the API for runs of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the head SHA. For a `pull_request` event the run executes the PR merge ref's copy of that file, so the workflow object / `path` is the real CI one no matter what the file's contents are. Attack: an `agent:managed` human PR (explicitly on this promote path per the panel gate at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:164-169, which only excludes forks) pushes a branch whose `ci.yml` runs no tests — or one that adds a `workflow_dispatch` trigger and then dispatches a green run with a higher `id` than the real red `pull_request` run, defeating newest-wins without touching the trigger tripwire's own execution. Either way gate 1 reads `success` and the PR is flipped to ready with a hand-off comment asserting "CI verification (`verify:self` and `verify:integration`) is green" (mark-ready.mjs:271). Mitigations: the attacker needs repo write (to push `.github/workflows/**` and to apply `agent:managed`), the agent App itself cannot push workflow files, and branch protection still requires a human approving review before merge — so this is a weakened gate rather than a merge bypass. The delta documents the gap honestly (mark-ready.mjs:16-25, harness-engineering.md:1941-1948) but leaves it open while the surrounding text and the `stalled`/promote machinery keep treating gate 1 as separate-actor proof that the tests ran. Closing it means comparing the run's workflow content (or the diff's `.github/workflows/**` touch) against the base branch.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts gate 1's "which file ran, not what was in it" gap is left open and only documented. In this tree it is closed by an enforced gate 1b: mark-ready.mjs:175 defines CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES ([".github/workflows/", ".github/actions/"]), branchEditsCiDefinition (:181-195) checks both filename and previous_filename across paginated PR files, ranBaseCiDefinition (:197-208) fails closed on an unreadable list, and ciDefinitionGate (:210) is computed unconditionally and folded into gates (:238) and allOk (:251) — so a branch touching .github/workflows/** exits 1 and is never flipped to ready (:253-256). Both claimed attacks require editing ci.yml (ci.yml:6-28 has only push/pull_request/merge_group, so adding workflow_dispatch is itself a workflow edit), and both are caught. The quoted hand-off text is also not as described: mark-ready.mjs:320-322 explicitly states "and the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on main rather than one the branch supplied." Tests pin the behaviour (mark-ready.test.mjs:262-299: ci.yml, another workflow, a composite action, a rename out of the directory, and an unreadable file list all exit 1 with no promotion; a code-only PR still promotes). Promotion has one entry point — `gh pr ready` appears only at mark-ready.mjs:276, invoked solely from agent-review-panel.yml:1508 — so there is no unguarded call site.
